newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Alliance would lower Telecom prices.
newsitem.headline: NZ Alliance would lower Telecom prices.

text.p: New Zealand Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Tuesday that Telecom Corp Chairman Peter Shirtcliffe was right to be afraid of the Alliance.
In a press release headlined "Anderton to Shirtcliffe: Be afraid. Be very, very afraid", Anderton said the Alliance would lower Telecom's prices if it won power at the October 12 general election.
"You bet we're going to push down Telecom's prices," Anderton said, responding to an interview Shirtcliffe gave to Reuters in Sydney in which he singled out the Alliance for criticism.
Anderton said Telecom was "exploiting a dominant market position, and ordinary New Zealand residential customers and businesses are paying the price through excessive line charges".
Anderton said Shirtcliffe's "disingenuous claim that Telecom is cross-subsidising its residential lines is a joke".
"If the residential lines are such a burden, the Alliance will happily take them off Telecom's hands," Anderton said.

"The reality is that Telecom attributes costs to the residential network that should be placed elsewhere in the company's structure. The Alliance will force Telecom to open its books so that everyone can see how fairly the costs are allocated."
Anderton described Shirtcliffe's use of the term "control freaks" to describe the Alliance as "ironic".

"Telecom controls the telecommunications market for its own gain. It uses the telephone numbering system to undermine potential competitors. That is why the Alliance is going to take the numbering system away from Telecom.
"When Mr Shirtcliffe warns other businesses that if it is us today, it'll be you tomorrow' he has a good point. The Alliance will pursue any other greedy monopolist just as vigorously.
"I'm glad Telecom has woken up to the fact that the Alliance has it in its sights. If the company is worried now, it can rest assured its troubles have only just begun."

Anderton reissued a challenge, declined by Shirtcliffe last weekend, to debate the issues with him, and offered to go to Sydney "to debate them in front of his Australian business friends". -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
